text:
Mornings don't usually feel this mild in late October, and it's only going to get warmer: we're clear and 50 already, with sunshine and a south breeze pushing us to a high near 65 this afternoon. That breeze runs 12 to 16 mph with gusts close to 30, and with all the dry leaves around, fire danger is elevated. A special weather statement is in effect until 8:15 tonight, so skip the backyard burning.

A weak cold front brings clouds and a slight chance of a few showers between 8 and 10 tonight. NWS and the American model barely see it, but the European model is much wetter, so tuck an umbrella nearby if you're out this evening. Even then, we're talking a few hundredths up to a tenth of an inch, nowhere near a soaking. Tonight stays mild, around 49.

Friday turns cooler behind the front, partly sunny with a high near 56 and a northwest breeze gusting to about 25. Saturday is sunny and cooler yet, mid 40s to low 50s, so Halloween trick-or-treaters want a layer under the costume. Wear a jacket Friday, and enjoy today's warmth while it lasts.

  Thursday: Sunny, with a high near 65. South wind 12 to 16 mph, with gusts as high as 29 mph.

  Friday: Partly sunny, with a high near 56. Northwest wind 7 to 14 mph, with gusts as high as 25 mph.
AFD KEY MESSAGES (forecaster's reasoning, issued 2026-10-29T06:25:00+00:00 — covers the whole BTV area, northern NY included: translate to what Burlington feels, never repeat other regions' place names):
  1. Warm and breezy conditions expected across the region today ahead of a weak cold front. Some light rain showers will be possible tonight into Friday, with drier conditions returning for the weekend.
  2. Increased fire weather concerns through this weekend.
  3. November will begin with dry, above normal temperatures, and remaining uncertain for the timing of precipitation in a week.
AFD WHAT CHANGED (same regional caveat): As of 224 AM EDT Thursday... No significant changes have been made to the forecast.
AFD DISCUSSION (the forecaster's full reasoning, same regional caveat; their temps are area-wide ranges):
KEY MESSAGE 1: A warm and breezy day is expected across the region today as southerly flow continues to usher in milder conditions. Afternoon high temperatures look to climb into the 60s areawide, with a few locations even nearing 70 degrees. A weak cold front will move through the region late today, bringing the potential for some light rain showers. The combination of weak forcing and some dry air to overcome will limit rainfall amounts, with most locations only observing a few hundreths of an inch. Strong cold air advection looks to take place on Friday behind the front, with increased clouds and some chances for showers in the favored upslope areas. Temperatures on Friday will be more seasonable, with highs in the upper 40s and 50s. Heading into the weekend, surface high pressure looks to build into the region once again. This will lead to another stretch of dry weather, with ample sunshine, light winds, and pleasant conditions to round out October and welcome the start of November. Temperatures on Saturday will be a little on the cooler side, with highs generally in the mid 40s to low 50s. KEY MESSAGE 2: Breezy winds and lower relative humidity values will lead to increased fire weather concerns over the next few days, especially given the plentiful dry leaves serving as fuel. Wind gusts today and Friday will generally be in the 15 to 25 mph range, with some higher gusts are possible. The highest winds gusts this afternoon are expected in the St. Lawrence Valley and northern slopes of the Adirondacks where gusts up to 35 mph are possible. Minimum relative humidity values will generally be between 40 to 55 percent for both today and Friday. Heading into the weekend, minimum relative humidity values should drop into the 30 to 45 percent range, but winds look to be much lighter. A weak front moves through the region later today, bringing some light rain showers however a wetting rainfall is not expected. KEY MESSAGE 3: Surface high pressure will shift offshore, but mid-level ridging will remain in place. Temperatures will move towards above seasonal norms, which is generally upper 40s to lower 50s during the day, and mid 20s to mid 30s at night as we enter into November. Instead, we'll have mid 50s to lower 60s during the days, and then mid 30s to mid 40s at night. A cold front is going to try to sink southwards Monday afternoon into Tuesday, but the upper vort is going to abandon the boundary and race east instead. So without cold air backing up the boundary and meager moisture, it may generate a few light rain showers, but that's about it. The pattern becomes increasingly uncertain after next Tuesday as a compact, but a strong upper low will begion to take shape in the Plains. The question is whether it completely cuts off from the jet stream or if it quickly gets absorbed back into the mid-latitude westerlies. Increasing ridging across the high latitudes will be present, and so this will likely keeps things moving slowly. Assessing forecast

WCAX METEOROLOGIST (regional station — Burlington relevance only, never their branding): BURLINGTON, Vt. (WCAX) -You’ll notice that Thursday morning feels better and warmer than that of Wednesday morning. We look to continue that warming trend into Thursday afternoon as most climb towards the low and even mid 60s. We do have a bit of a breeze out of the south helping to warm us up. That, combined with all the sunshine, dry and dead leaves and grass, means fire danger is high for the day ahead. A few clouds may begin to build in through Thursday, and could give way to a few showers Thursday evening into Thursday night. Any rain we see is not all that impressive, with most only running up to a tenth of an inch. Any rain should be wrapping up by Friday morning, but we may hang onto a bit more cloud cover through Friday with high temperatures in the upper 50s to lower 60s. The weekend forecast at this point is not looking too bad. Saturday for Halloween features nice sunshine, but temperatures are cooler in the 40s. Trick-or-treat time remains clear as temperatures fall through the 40s back into the 30s, so the kiddos may want an extra layer over the costume. Don’t forget we fall back one hour Saturday night into Sunday. Sunday features more sunshine with high temperatures in the 50s. There is a chance for maybe a few hit-or-miss showers into Monday, with temperatures again in the 50s to about 60 for Monday afternoon. There is a chance for a spotty shower or two, but most will likely stay dry. Tuesday again features more clouds and a chance for a spotty shower, with high temperatures in the 50s to about 60. The better chance of rain finally comes towards the end of next week, but that is still several days out. We will be keeping an eye on it.
NBC5 METEOROLOGIST (2026-10-28T22:25:00Z — same caveat): Mild and breezy Thursday — Thursday turns warmer, as a gusty south breeze sends highs to around 70. Expect lots of sunshine through the morning and afternoon. A cold front brings a band of clouds and spotty showers during the evening, lasting into the overnight. Friday turns mostly dry, with only a spot shower leftover. However, expect more clouds than sun with highs falling back to the 50s. Halloween weekend starts bright but cool on Saturday, with highs in the upper 40s. Sunday turns a bit milder, with highs in the mid-50s, as sun mixes with clouds. Most of next week looks mild for early November, with highs pushing past 60 several days in a row. Monday looks brightest, then more clouds and a greater chance for showers arrive by mid to late week.
